experience.title: Analyst Programmer Intern
experience.one_line: Built an LLM-plus-fuzzy-matching pipeline that extracts and canonicalizes the four counterparties on a commercial insurance risk out of unstructured policy documents.
experience.problem: Commercial insurance processing depends on correctly identifying four distinct parties on every risk: Named Insured, Underwriter, Broker, and Reinsurer. Two failure modes break rule-based parsers. First, role ambiguity: brokers and underwriters are both company names in similar syntactic positions, so position-based rules guess wrong whenever a document deviates from house style. Second, naming variance: 'Acme Corp', 'Acme Corporation LLC', and 'Acme Inc.' are one counterparty that a regex parser records as three.
approach: Split the problem into a probabilistic half and a deterministic half: an LLM reads context to assign roles, then a deterministic fuzzy matcher canonicalizes each extracted name against reference master data.

Chose few-shot prompting over fine-tuning a domain NER model (spaCy/BERT) because the bottleneck was contextual role disambiguation, not pattern recognition, and no labelled corpus of sufficient size existed within the project timeline.

Schema-first prompt design: explicit field definitions for the four roles, plus 3-5 exemplars curated specifically for documents where a broker and an underwriter appear within a few words of each other.
Constrained JSON output so responses parse deterministically and a malformed generation fails loudly instead of silently corrupting downstream records.
Normalization layer: punctuation stripping, case folding, and legal-suffix truncation (Inc., LLC, GmbH) for comparison only, preserving the original string for audit.
Similarity scoring with Levenshtein distance and token-sort ratio, catching both character-level typos and reordered word forms.

Banded thresholds converting a continuous score into three explicit outcomes: at or above 85% auto-links to a canonical ID, 60-85% is flagged for human validation, and below that no match is asserted.

Synthetic evaluation benchmark generated to mirror real multi-party schedules, endorsements, and slips, avoiding any exposure of PII or PHI while giving known ground truth and controllable edge cases.
methods: Few-shot LLM named entity recognition (Azure OpenAI)
Fuzzy string matching (Levenshtein distance, token-sort ratio)
Entity resolution and canonical ID linkage

results.note: Measured in subsequent policy-processing steps after canonicalized output was integrated.

key_findings: Few-shot prompting produced its largest gains precisely where rule-based parsing failed: sentences containing both a broker and an underwriter in close proximity.
Canonicalization collapsed name variants that had previously entered the data store as separate counterparties, removing duplicate records rather than merely relabeling them.
The operational value landed downstream: normalized output cut structural parse errors in later processing by roughly 15%.
deliverables: Streamlit reviewer interface with upload, side-by-side inspection, and approval flags
experience.research_relevance: A concrete study in where a language model should and should not be trusted: probabilistic extraction bounded by deterministic verification, with an explicit abstain band instead of a forced decision.
experience.confidentiality: Commercial work. Methods and the synthetic-benchmark metrics are shareable; do not reference client documents or real policy data.
talking_points: Why banded confidence thresholds beat a single cutoff: they make abstention an explicit, auditable outcome.
Why synthetic evaluation data was the right call given PII/PHI constraints, and what it costs in external validity.
The tradeoff between few-shot prompting and fine-tuning when labelled data is the binding constraint.

experience.title: Undergraduate Research Intern
experience.organization: Department of Computer Science and Engineering, IIT Kharagpur
experience.one_line: Built an end-to-end speech-to-text system for Vedic Sanskrit, from corpus construction through HuBERT-CTC fine-tuning and language-model decoding, reaching 17.5% WER and 6.2% CER.
experience.problem: Vedic Sanskrit is preserved through recitation, and pitch accent is meaning-bearing. In text this appears as svara markers (udatta U+0951, anudatta U+0952, the vowel sign U+0962) alongside characters such as the sacred syllable OM and the danda. Off-the-shelf ASR systems target modern Hindi or standard Sanskrit and cannot emit these symbols at all, because a CTC model can only predict tokens present in its output layer. Stripping the markers to fit an existing vocabulary discards exactly the information a Vedic transcript exists to record. Compounding this, no usable public audio-text corpus existed for this register.
approach: Corpus construction: scraped and consolidated verse transcripts into a single UTF-8 Devanagari corpus of roughly 30,785 verse lines, then paired recitation audio clip-by-clip with verse text into a mapping of 30,779 rows.
Splits of 24,623 train / 3,078 validation / 3,078 test, with clips over 30 seconds filtered out to bound activation memory on a single GPU; all audio decoded to mono 16 kHz.
Svara-preserving normalization: removed Latin and Devanagari digits, scraping-artifact punctuation, and redundant whitespace, while leaving every accent mark untouched.

Character-level tokenizer derived from the corpus itself (sorted unique characters plus [UNK], [PAD], and a word-delimiter), yielding a 74-token vocabulary regenerable from the text at any time. Character-level rather than word-level because Vedic vocabulary is effectively open and word units guarantee out-of-vocabulary failure.

Output vocabulary expansion: the pre-trained checkpoint inherits a 64-token output head from facebook/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53 containing none of the accent characters. Passing vocab_size=74 with ignore_mismatched_sizes=True re-initializes the CTC classification head at the larger size while loading every pre-trained encoder weight unchanged, so the head learns the new svara symbols during fine-tuning and the acoustic representation is inherited intact.
Dataset verification: an exact-match audit re-checked every training transcript against the canonical mapping, writing a full results table and an isolated mismatch file.

Fine-tuning HubertForCTC in an explicit PyTorch training loop rather than the Hugging Face Trainer, for control over per-epoch evaluation, logging, checkpointing, and memory behaviour on a shared cluster.
Two decoding paths evaluated on the same held-out split: greedy CTC argmax, and a KenLM 4-gram language model through a pyctcdecode beam decoder wrapped in an LM-aware processor.

training_configuration.architecture: 24 transformer layers, hidden size 1024, 16 attention heads, 7-layer convolutional feature encoder
training_configuration.objective: Connectionist Temporal Classification, mean loss reduction, 74-token character vocabulary
training_configuration.optimizer: AdamW, learning rate 1e-5, linear schedule with 1,500 warmup steps
training_configuration.memory: Gradient checkpointing, frozen convolutional feature encoder, periodic CUDA cache flush
training_configuration.regularization: Attention and hidden dropout 0.1, layerdrop 0.1, SpecAugment time-mask probability 0.05

results.note: Held-out Vedic test split, 3,074 scored clips.
Baseline reference: a Hindi XLSR model probed on Common Voice Hindi.

key_findings: The gap between 6.2% CER and 17.5% WER indicates the acoustic model resolves phonemes well and that most word-level errors come from a small number of characters, specifically accent marks and sandhi boundaries, rather than from wholesale mishearing.

Verification found 14,625 of 24,623 training rows (approximately 59%) disagreed with the canonical mapping. This places a hard ceiling on achievable WER and identifies alignment, not architecture, as the highest-leverage remaining problem.
Output-head resizing is the mechanism that makes Vedic transcription possible at all; without it the accent characters are structurally undecodable regardless of training.
limitations_stated_honestly: Trained checkpoints were retained in project cloud storage rather than published.
Dependencies were unpinned and paths were cluster-absolute, so the code is not reproducible as-is on another machine.
The transcript mismatch was quantified but not resolved within the internship.
experience.research_relevance: The closest thing I have to sustained research work, and the direct basis for my interest in low-resource speech. It covers the whole loop: corpus construction, script-aware normalization, architectural adaptation, and evaluation, on a language where none of it existed beforehand.
talking_points: Why the output head had to be resized from 64 to 74 tokens, and what that implies for adapting pre-trained ASR to any script with unrepresented characters.
Why character-level CTC is the right choice for an open-vocabulary liturgical language.
What the CER-to-WER gap says about where the remaining errors actually live.
Why quantifying the 59% transcript mismatch was more valuable than quietly training through it.

Content-aware SQLite/aiosqlite cache with configurable TTL so repeat runs are deterministic and avoid redundant paid calls.
Gmail API sender with OAuth refresh, MIME/base64url encoding, UTF-8 preservation, and CR/LF header-injection sanitization, gated behind a send_enabled kill-switch.

projects.title: Agentic Inventory-Replenishment POC
projects.one_line: A deterministic six-agent LangGraph pipeline that turns a stock breach into the correct purchasing action, with the language model structurally excluded from every decision path.
projects.problem: A demand planner at an automotive-parts distributor must scan hundreds of SKUs each morning and decide who to buy from, what quantity to order, and which orders require human approval. The work is high-volume, policy-driven, and audit-bound, which makes it a poor fit for an unconstrained LLM agent.
approach: Six-agent LangGraph state graph: stock_monitor, demand_forecast, vendor_checker, approval, then a three-way fork to po_generator, human_approval, or notification.

Three-way autonomy fork (AUTO-ISSUE, DRAFT-FOR-APPROVAL, SUPPRESS) with a real LangGraph interrupt pause on the draft path, so a draft physically cannot reach the purchase-order node without an explicit human resume command.

The LLM is restricted to two human-facing text edges only, the draft justification narrative and the notification body, behind a Gemini to Ollama to deterministic-template fallback chain that never raises. Detection, forecasting, and routing are deterministic Python.
Append-only audit log enforced at the database level via SQLite triggers that abort UPDATE and DELETE, with a single append_audit writer chokepoint.
Structural write guardrail: one _write_allowed check plus required-field validation refuses any purchase order missing vendor, quantity, or approver.
Vendor-consolidated batch purchase orders collapsing N per-SKU orders into one order per shared approved vendor, with supplier eligibility and minimum-order-quantity gating.
Demand sizing applying promotional and seasonal uplifts multiplicatively over a weekly baseline, ceil-rounded to pack size.
Byte-stable determinism from a fixed random seed and reference date, so all routing decisions reproduce identically on any machine.

results.value: 18 pytest cases across guardrails, audit, HITL, and graph suites, all passing
4 (auto-issue, draft-pause, batch consolidation, suppress), reproducing byte-stable from a fixed seed

projects.research_relevance: An argument, in code, that reliable agentic systems come from restricting the model's authority rather than improving its prompts. The autonomy tiers and the structural write guard are the interesting part, not the LLM.
